about.title: About
about.lead: Shashlik.Master assembles a marinade recipe based on your meat, style and fat preferences.

howItWorks.label: HOW IT WORKS
howItWorks.step1: Pick meat, style, intensity, fat and spiciness.
howItWorks.step2: The algorithm picks required spices and random style spices respecting compatibility and conflicts.
howItWorks.step3: Final amounts are computed from meat type, intensity and fat coefficients.

stack.label: STACK
stack.line1: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite, framer-motion for animations.
stack.line2: i18next for RU/EN locales, vitest for unit tests of the core.

steps.mixDry: Mix dry spices in a separate bowl.
steps.combine: Add onion, salt and pepper, then fold in the rest.
steps.recommendedTime: Recommended marinating time for this meat: {{time}}.
steps.dryBeforeGrill: Before grilling, drain excess marinade and pat the meat dry.

caucasus.marinade: Crush onion with salt until juicy, then fold in dry spices and your chosen acid.
caucasus.layer: Pack the marinade tightly against the meat so it stays in contact.

turkish.marinade: Whisk yogurt or cultured dairy with sumac and dry spices until smooth.
turkish.layer: Coat evenly; add fresh herbs at the very end of mixing.

eastern.marinade: Toast dry spices in a dry pan for 30 seconds, cool, then blend with the wet base.
eastern.layer: Submerge the meat and press under a lid in the fridge.

spicy.marinade: Mix hot and smoky spices separately, then combine with the rest of the base.
spicy.layer: Rub thoroughly into the fibers; break up any pepper clumps.

premium.marinade: Build in layers: oil and citrus first, then herbs and salt.
premium.layer: Pack tightly in a container with the marinade clinging to the meat.

herbal.marinade: Crush dry herbs lightly; add fresh herbs last to preserve aroma.
herbal.layer: Keep the marinade cool; avoid overheating delicate greens.

express.marinade: Quickly mix all dry parts, then immediately fold in liquid and meat.
express.layer: Let stand briefly at room temperature before chilling.

classic.tip1: Coals should wear a white ash coat; cook on moderate heat and flip less often.
classic.tip2: Check doneness by juice in the fibers; avoid extra slashes.

caucasus.tip1: Moderate embers suit Caucasus-style marinades; avoid aggressive flame-ups.
caucasus.tip2: Rest off the heat 3–5 minutes under foil before serving.

turkish.tip1: Yogurt marinades brown fast—do not scorch the first flip.
turkish.tip2: Serve with lemon wedges and fresh herbs.

eastern.tip1: Watch caramelization from sugar or honey—slightly hotter than medium can burn.
eastern.tip2: Turmeric and pepper tint the crust; trust aroma as well as time.

spicy.tip1: Spicy marinades darken quickly—keep a little distance from the coals.
spicy.tip2: Creamy sauces after grilling tame heat at the table.

premium.tip1: Citrus-herb premium mixes prefer moderate heat and fewer flips.
premium.tip2: Pull slightly early—it carries over while resting.

herbal.tip1: Herbs scorch fast—use a higher rack or indirect heat.
herbal.tip2: Keep finishing herbs off the fire until plating.

express.tip1: With short marination, do not start on maximum heat.
express.tip2: If the surface dries, a light oil wipe on the grate helps.
